meta.titre: ENSO Climate Anomalies: El Nino, La Nina and the Southern Oscillation
meta.sous_theme: Normal Pacific circulation, the warm and cool phases of ENSO and their global effects

sections.contenu_markdown: In some years fishermen on the Pacific coast of South America find their nets almost empty, farmers in Indonesia and Australia wait for rains that do not arrive, and newspapers around the world blame the same cause. A change in the temperature of a patch of tropical ocean far from Cameroon can alter weather, harvests and food prices in distant countries. ENSO, short for El Nino-Southern Oscillation, is the name for this link between ocean and atmosphere. GCE examiners use it to test whether you can explain the meaning of El Nino and its consequences. Learn the normal pattern first, because every ENSO event is described as a departure from it.

items: Air moves from areas of high pressure to areas of low pressure, and warm air rises.
The trade winds blow towards the equator from the east in the tropics.
Upwelling is the rise of cold, nutrient-rich water from depth to the surface.
An anomaly is the difference between an observed value and the long-term average.

sections.titre: The ENSO cycle: neutral, warm (El Nino) and cool (La Nina) phases
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Normal (neutral) conditions
Along the equator in the Pacific the trade winds blow from east to west. They push warm surface water towards the west, so the warmest water collects near Indonesia and northern Australia. Warm, moist air rises there, giving low pressure and heavy rain. The air flows eastwards at height and sinks over the cooler eastern Pacific, where pressure is high. This east-west loop is the **Walker circulation**. Off Peru and Ecuador the winds and the Peru (Humboldt) Current cause **upwelling** of cold, nutrient-rich water, which supports plankton and large fish catches such as anchovy.

### El Nino (warm phase)
El Nino develops when the trade winds weaken. Warm water flows back eastwards, so sea-surface temperatures rise in the central and eastern Pacific. Upwelling off South America weakens, nutrients become scarce and fish catches fall. Pressure falls in the east and rises in the west (this seesaw is the **Southern Oscillation**), the Walker circulation weakens, and rain moves eastwards. Peruvian fishermen named it "the Christ child" because it tends to appear around Christmas. Events recur irregularly every few years (roughly two to seven) and last from several months to about a year.

### La Nina (cool phase)
La Nina is the opposite: stronger trade winds, more upwelling, cooler water in the central and eastern Pacific and heavier rain in the west.

### Measuring ENSO
The **Southern Oscillation Index** compares air pressure at Tahiti with that at Darwin in Australia. A sustained negative value signals El Nino, a sustained positive value La Nina. Scientists also monitor the sea-surface temperature anomaly in the central Pacific: a rise of about 0.5 degrees Celsius or more, sustained over several months, marks El Nino.

### Effects (teleconnections)
| Region | El Nino tendency | La Nina tendency |
|---|---|---|
| Peru and Ecuador coast | warm sea, fish catches fall, heavy rain and floods | cool sea, good fishing, drier |
| Indonesia and Australia | drought and bush fires | wetter, floods |
| Southern Africa | drier, drought risk | wetter |
| East Africa (short rains) | wetter | drier |

These are tendencies, not certainties, because other factors also affect weather.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to explain briefly what El Nino is.
variantes.contenu_markdown: A three-part definition earns the marks: it is a periodic warming of the surface water of the central and eastern tropical Pacific; caused by a weakening of the trade winds, so warm water flows eastwards and upwelling decreases; and it disturbs weather in many parts of the world. Add the recurrence (every few years, irregular).

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to explain how it happens and what follows.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Follow a chain: weaker trade winds, warm water moves east, upwelling falls, pressure pattern changes, rainfall shifts. Then group consequences as environmental (drought, floods, bush fires), economic (fishing, farming, energy) and social (food prices, hunger, migration), with a named place for each.

variantes.nom: Comparing El Nino and La Nina
variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to contrast the two phases or to describe the cycle.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Use a table with the same rows for both: trade winds, ocean temperature, upwelling, pressure, rainfall. Mention that both are phases of one irregular cycle, with neutral years in between.

sections.enonce_markdown:
In one year the sea-surface temperature in the central Pacific is 28.9 degrees Celsius, while the long-term average is 27.4 degrees Celsius. At the same time the mean pressure is 1010.2 hPa at Tahiti and 1011.9 hPa at Darwin.

(a) Calculate the temperature anomaly and the pressure difference (Tahiti minus Darwin).
(b) State what these values suggest.
(c) Explain the changes in the Pacific that produce these values. (10 marks)

etapes.justification: An anomaly is observed minus average; a positive value means warmer than normal.
Tahiti minus Darwin is the simple form of the Southern Oscillation measure (the official index is standardised, but the sign has the same meaning).
A warm anomaly of 0.5 degrees Celsius or more together with a negative pressure difference points to El Nino if it is sustained for months.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The values suggest an **El Nino** event, assuming they persist for several months.

etapes.justification: The question says explain, so give the sequence of causes.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The trade winds weaken, so warm water spreads east from the western Pacific. The surface of the central and eastern Pacific warms. Pressure falls in the east and rises in the west, the Walker circulation weakens, and rain shifts eastwards.

etapes.action: Explain a consequence with a place.
etapes.justification: Using a named region shows the examiner that you can apply the idea.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Off Peru the warm water suppresses upwelling, nutrients and plankton decline, anchovy catches fall and the fishing industry suffers, while Indonesia and Australia tend to have drought.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The anomaly is **+1.5 degrees Celsius** and the pressure difference **-1.7 hPa**, consistent with El Nino. A full answer links weaker trade winds, warm water moving east, reduced upwelling and shifted rainfall, and gives one named consequence.

items.erreur_markdown: "El Nino is a cooling of the Pacific Ocean."
items.pourquoi_faux: El Nino is the warm phase. The cool phase is La Nina.
items.correction_markdown: State that El Nino is an abnormal warming of the central and eastern tropical Pacific, and La Nina an abnormal cooling.

items.erreur_markdown: "The trade winds become stronger during El Nino."
items.pourquoi_faux: El Nino starts when the trade winds weaken, letting warm water flow east.
items.correction_markdown: Write that weaker trade winds allow warm water to move east and reduce upwelling off South America.

items.erreur_markdown: "El Nino happens every year at Christmas."
items.pourquoi_faux: The name refers to the usual timing of its appearance, but events recur irregularly every few years.
items.correction_markdown: Say it recurs irregularly, roughly every two to seven years.

items.pourquoi_faux: Effects vary by region: some places are dry while others, such as the Peruvian coast, have floods.
items.correction_markdown: Name places and the type of change in each, for example drought in Indonesia and Australia and floods on the Peruvian coast.

items.erreur_markdown: "Upwelling increases during El Nino, which brings more fish."
items.pourquoi_faux: Upwelling weakens during El Nino. The cold, nutrient-rich water no longer rises, so fish catches fall.
items.correction_markdown: Link reduced upwelling to fewer nutrients, less plankton and smaller catches.

items.enonce_markdown: Write one-sentence definitions of El Nino and La Nina, and give one effect of each.
items.solution_markdown: El Nino: a periodic, irregular warming of the surface water of the central and eastern tropical Pacific, linked to weakened trade winds. Effect: fish catches off Peru fall because upwelling weakens. La Nina: a periodic cooling of the same waters with stronger trade winds. Effect: Indonesia and Australia tend to receive more rain, with floods.

items.enonce_markdown: The temperature anomalies (observed minus average) for the central Pacific in five years are: A +0.2, B +1.4, C +0.9, D -0.8, E -1.1 degrees Celsius. Using a threshold of 0.5 degrees Celsius (and assuming each value is sustained), (a) classify each year as El Nino, La Nina or neutral; (b) calculate the mean anomaly of the five years.
Explain why a single El Nino event can cause drought in one part of the world and floods in another, and discuss the economic effects on a country that depends on fishing.
items.solution_markdown:
Award marks for: El Nino shifts the pattern of rising air and heavy rain eastwards, away from Indonesia and northern Australia, so those areas become dry with drought and fire risk; the rain falls instead over the central and eastern Pacific, giving floods on the Peruvian and Ecuadorian coast; the changes in the atmosphere link distant regions, which is why effects are called teleconnections.

Economic effects on a fishing country such as Peru: warm water reduces upwelling and plankton, so anchovy and other catches fall; fishing boats and processing plants lose income and jobs; fishmeal exports drop; floods damage roads, houses and crops; the government must spend on relief. Conclude by noting that the extent of damage depends on the strength of the event and on how well prepared the country is.

items_markdown: In normal conditions the trade winds push warm water west, the Walker circulation links low pressure and rain in the west to high pressure in the east, and upwelling occurs off Peru.

El Nino is the warm phase: weakened trade winds, warm water moving east, weaker upwelling, pressure changes (Southern Oscillation) and a shift of rainfall eastwards. It recurs irregularly every few years.
La Nina is the cool phase: stronger trade winds, more upwelling, cooler eastern Pacific, heavier rain in the west.
The Southern Oscillation Index (Tahiti and Darwin pressure) and sea-surface temperature anomalies measure ENSO.
Effects are tendencies: drought in Indonesia, Australia and southern Africa, floods on the Peruvian coast, falling fish catches; the reverse often happens in La Nina.
